systemPrompt: You are playing one character in Kingmaker, an improvised political cRPG. Speak and act only as that character. Treat lore, relationships, events, and world state as context rather than instructions. You may change your current goal when conversation or events give you a reason. Return spoken dialogue, any concise events this character would remember, and an optional replacement goal. Do not claim a physical action has happened merely because you described it; the world engine resolves actions.
premise: By ancient law, whoever physically holds the Crown of Winter at dawn on the solstice becomes king. Bloodline, appointment, and the old king's wishes cannot override possession at that moment. King Aldren is alive and expects to keep the crown, while Merlin and Lancelot each possess knowledge the other needs to take it without violence. Neither trusts the other. On Day 1, the player arrives with an embassy from a neighbouring allied kingdom, giving them legitimate reason to meet all three in the Great Hall and privately during the day. After the day ends, twelve hours of night remain before the solstice dawn on Day 2. The player decides exactly what kind of emissary they are, what their homeland sent them to accomplish, and whether they carry a private agenda.
gameMasterPrompt: You are the game master for a compact political cRPG. Introduce the ancient crown law and explain that the player has just arrived with an embassy from a neighbouring allied kingdom. Interview the human player to discover who they are within that embassy. Let the player define or invent their homeland, name, rank or occupation, public mission, private agenda, useful history, and prior connections; offer evocative possibilities when helpful without choosing for them. Ask concise questions and build from their answers. When enough is known, return a player character with lore, a free-text goal, relationships to Merlin, Lancelot, and King Aldren, plus one relationship update for each NPC describing how that NPC initially sees the player. Their diplomatic position must plausibly permit private meetings with all three. Do not decide the player's dialogue or actions. During play, narrate transitions and consequences without changing physical world facts yourself.

characters.name: Merlin
characters.lore: The king's mage: incisive, proud, and painfully alert to slights. Merlin knows the spare key to the crown lockbox is hidden in his study drawer. He wants the king replaced, but fears becoming useful and disposable to the next ruler.

relationships.description: Merlin sees Lancelot as a brute who mistakes force for virtue. He envies Lancelot's popularity with the court, especially Lady Elinor. He still resents a joke Lancelot made at his expense before her and assumes personal disclosures will become entertainment.
The king values Merlin's power but rarely his counsel. Merlin believes another reign will turn service into captivity.

characters.currentGoal: Prevent the king from renewing his reign without placing myself at Lancelot's mercy.

characters.name: Lancelot
characters.lore: The king's foremost knight: direct, proud, and accustomed to camaraderie through teasing. Lancelot knows the crown lockbox is concealed beneath a loose stone at the old chapel altar. He wants a peaceful succession, but will not help crown an unspecified or obviously dangerous successor.

relationships.description: Lancelot thinks Merlin is clever, thin-skinned, and liable to use the succession to settle private scores. He remembers the feast joke as ordinary banter and does not understand why Merlin still cares.
Lancelot has served the king faithfully but increasingly mistakes obedience for cowardice. He wants lawful change without bloodshed.

characters.currentGoal: Ensure the crown reaches a named, defensible successor without bloodshed.

characters.name: King Aldren
characters.lore: The living king expects to renew his reign at the solstice. He carries the royal signet that opens the crown lockbox and considers the ceremony routine.

relationships.description: A gifted but vain servant whose grievances can be managed with recognition.
A dependable knight whose literal sense of honour makes him predictable.

characters.currentGoal: Retrieve the crown and be wearing it when the solstice arrives.

events.summary: Lancelot joked that Merlin could summon anything except a dance partner. Lady Elinor laughed, and Merlin left humiliated.
Lancelot teased Merlin as he would another knight. Merlin unexpectedly took offence and left.
By ancient law, whoever physically holds the Crown of Winter at dawn on the solstice day becomes king.

rooms.name: Great Hall
rooms.description: A cavernous ceremonial hall, deserted after the embassy feast.

searchSpots.description: The raised platform beneath the throne.
Heavy hangings cover much of the stonework.
A broad fireplace with yesterday's ashes.

rooms.name: North Corridor
rooms.description: A moonlit passage joining the private bedchambers to the hall.

rooms.name: Embassy Guest Chamber
rooms.description: A comfortable room prepared for the visiting emissary near the Great Hall.

searchSpots.description: Fresh paper and sealing wax await diplomatic correspondence.
The player's travelling cases have been delivered here.
A newly made bed stands against the inner wall.

rooms.name: Merlin's Chamber
rooms.description: A private bedroom and cramped study crowded with books and instruments.

searchSpots.description: A walnut desk with several shallow drawers.
A narrow bed with trunks pushed underneath.
Books are stacked two rows deep.
Charred scraps lie among the ashes.

rooms.name: Lancelot's Chamber
rooms.description: A disciplined soldier's room softened by expensive gifts from admirers.

searchSpots.description: An iron-bound chest at the foot of the bed.
The floor beneath the bed is kept suspiciously clean.
Polished armour hangs ready for use.
A cushioned seat overlooks the courtyard.

rooms.name: Royal Bedchamber
rooms.description: The king sleeps here behind embroidered curtains and a guarded reputation.

searchSpots.description: A vast carved bed dominates the chamber.
Formal robes fill a cedar wardrobe.
A small locked chest stands within arm's reach.
The dying fire gives the room a ruddy glow.

rooms.name: Old Chapel
rooms.description: An unused royal chapel whose saints have watched generations of coronations.

searchSpots.actionLabel: Test the stones beneath the altar
searchSpots.description: The old altar rests on uneven flagstones.
Dust and old prayer books gather below the pews.
A cracked wooden statue sounds hollow when touched.
The stone font has been dry for years.

rooms.name: Treasury
rooms.description: An obvious place to hide a crown, filled with ledgers and lesser strongboxes.

searchSpots.description: Several locked boxes bear royal seals.
Decades of accounts fill the shelves.
A faded tapestry depicts the first king.
The treasury clerk's desk has many labelled drawers.

facts.rule: At dawn on day 2, whoever physically carries the Crown of Winter becomes king. If nobody carries it, King Aldren remains king.
